title: AI Voiced NPCs in a text-based game/MUD: do they add to it or get in the way? (video)
author: Embergloam
selftext:
I've been working with Claude to build a text-based MUD, figuring out screen effects, hit feel and a lot more without putting any images in the game itself (the website aside). It's been a really fun adventure!

It started small. I wanted to resurrect my old DikuMUD and prototype faster, more action-driven combat over telnet, with a HUD for health, mana, casts and your target: a couple of test rooms and one creature. Then I just kept going... thanks, Claude!

One thread I keep pulling on is audio that supports the text: music beds, combat themes, sound effects, weather. That started because I just wanted to hear rain when the game was actually raining.

Lately I've been thinking about audiobooks, and whether a MUD could add a voiced, immersive layer on top of everything else. It's in the High Elf starting area now (voices designed in ElevenLabs), and the plan is to expand it across the whole game as an optional setting.

**Spoiler warning:** the video is a held scene that brings all of this together, and it's a big story moment. If you might play, skip it. Otherwise, I'd love your thoughts on voiced moments like this when big story beats land.

**Biggest question:** do the AI NPC voices add to the experience or take away from it? Eleven v4 seems significantly more believable than v3.

More short clips of the game: [https://embergloam.com/#plays](https://embergloam.com/#plays)

comments.author: Embergloam
comments.body:
In the video I posted, I was trying to slow down the dragon's voice to sound less human but it just reads too slow / emotionless. Re-recorded with ElevenLabs as v4 to get more emotion -- still sounded too human, but was better than v3.

Then layered on a pitch-shifted copy of his voice under itself and now he sounds properly otherworldly. Great success!

New version: [The Green Rune](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QM1JwuJltB4)
